# nonFloat

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is **not** a number with a fractional part.</link-summary>

<web-summary>nonFloat() — Checks whether a value is **not** a number with a fractional part. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/number</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function nonFloat<T>(value: T | number): value is T;
```

`nonFloat(value)` is the same test as `!isFloat(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.

JavaScript has one numeric type, so `1.0` and `1` are the same value: the question answered is whether a fraction survives at runtime, not how the literal was written. The infinities have no fraction and are excluded.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type          | Description         |
| :-------- | :------------ | :------------------ |
| `value`   | `T \| number` | The value to check. |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` when the value is not a number with a fractional part; otherwise `false`.

In TypeScript the guard narrows `value` to `T` inside the branch.

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
nonFloat(42); // => true
nonFloat(1.0); // => true
nonFloat(Infinity); // => true
nonFloat("1.5"); // => true
nonFloat(1.5); // => false
nonFloat(-0.1); // => false
```
